questions.statement: My sister, ___ lives in Spain, is visiting us next week.
questions.context: A non-defining clause, which takes a comma and never that.

options.feedback: Correct! A non-defining clause uses who for a person and is set off by commas.
That is not used in a non-defining clause, because a restrictive meaning is what that always carries.
Which refers to things, and the antecedent is my sister.
What cannot be used with a preceding noun as an antecedent.

questions.explanation:
A non-defining clause adds extra information about an already identified person or thing. It is separated by commas and uses who, whom, whose or which, never that.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Maria, ___ brother works in Madrid, is a dentist.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a possessive pronoun.

options.feedback: Correct! Whose expresses the relationship between Maria and her brother inside a non-defining clause.
Who would be the subject of the clause, but the clause has no verb of its own.
That cannot introduce a non-defining clause and would wrongly restrict the name Maria.
Which cannot refer to a person, and the antecedent is Maria.

questions.explanation:
Whose works in both defining and non-defining clauses. In the non-defining form it simply adds a piece of extra information about the person named.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The novel, ___ was published in 1994, is taught in schools.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a thing.

options.feedback: Correct! Which is the pronoun used for things in a non-defining clause, with the comma marking it as extra information.
That is reserved for defining clauses and would wrongly restrict which novel is meant.
What cannot be preceded by a noun antecedent.
Who refers to people, and the antecedent is the novel.

questions.explanation:
The comma is what makes a clause non-defining. Which is the standard pronoun for a thing in that position, and that is excluded.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: She passed the exam, ___ surprised everybody in the room.
questions.context: A non-defining clause added to a whole clause rather than a noun.

options.feedback: Correct! Which can stand for an entire clause in a non-defining position, and the comma marks the extra comment.
It has no antecedent, and the whole preceding clause has not been turned into a noun.
This cannot introduce a relative clause, and it has no clear antecedent here.
That is used for defining clauses and would restrict the meaning in a way the comma denies.

questions.explanation:
A non-defining which can refer back to a whole clause rather than to a single noun. It then adds a comment about the entire statement.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The teacher, ___ we spoke to yesterday, is leaving the school.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a preposition at the end.

options.feedback: Correct! The formal object pronoun is the right form after a preposition that closes a non-defining clause.
Who would leave the clause without an object, because spoke needs one before to.
In English the preposition stays at the end of the clause, and to who is not a possible order.
That is excluded from non-defining clauses altogether.

questions.explanation:
When a non-defining clause ends in a preposition, whom is the correct pronoun in formal English. In everyday speech the clause is often avoided altogether.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Dr. Reyes, ___ I met at the conference, is an expert on volcanoes.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a person, with the pronoun as object.

options.feedback: Correct! The pronoun is the object of met, and the formal form is whom.
Who cannot be an object, and met needs an object in this sentence.
Which cannot refer to a person.
That is not available in a non-defining clause, and whom is the correct register here.

questions.explanation:
Whom is the object form of who and is used in formal English, particularly after a preposition. In everyday speech who is often used loosely, but that is not correct for an object.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The results, ___ by the review board, will be published in June.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a past participle, which is not possible with the comma form.

options.feedback: Correct! A non-defining clause is never reduced, so the participle appears with the full pronoun.
A reduced clause drops the pronoun, and that is in any case not used non-definingly.
Which approved would put the results in the subject position of the clause, which is wrong.
Being belongs to continuous passives and cannot serve as a reduced relative pronoun here.

questions.explanation:
Only defining clauses can be reduced to a participle. A non-defining clause keeps its full structure, because the information it adds is not essential to the noun.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Her parents, ___ in Choluteca, visit her every summer.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a place, formal version.

options.feedback: Correct! In everyday English a clause about a place is often written with the verb and no relative pronoun at all.
Which would refer to a thing rather than to a person, and it is a clumsy solution here.
Where replaces a place preposition, but the verb live already stands in the clause and does not need one.
Who would need a verb after it, and the verb is already present.

questions.explanation:
In non-defining clauses about place or time, English frequently omits the pronoun altogether and just keeps the verb. This is the ordinary conversational pattern.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The company, ___ factory is in Choluteca, employs four hundred people.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a possessive pronoun about an organisation.

options.feedback: Correct! Whose links the company to the factory as its possessor, and it is the right pronoun here.
Who would be the subject of a verb, and the clause has no verb of its own.
That is not used in a non-defining clause and would wrongly restrict which company is meant.
Which cannot express possession, and the relationship is that of owner to owned.

questions.explanation:
Whose expresses possession and works with people, places and organisations. The noun it modifies follows it directly, with no article or determiner in between.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: Who is the author of the book, ___ won the prize?
questions.context: A non-defining clause in a question.

options.feedback: Correct! Which refers back to the whole preceding clause, and the comma marks it as extra information.
That cannot be used non-definingly, and it would restrict the noun to one particular book.
What cannot be used after a clause has already been completed with its own question word.
It has no antecedent, because the preceding words form a clause and not a noun.

questions.explanation:
A non-defining which can follow a whole clause in a question as well as a statement. The extra information is what the question is really asking about.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: My brother, ___ is a lawyer, is visiting us.
questions.context: A non-defining clause that could be misunderstood without the comma.

options.feedback: Correct! Who is the subject of the clause, and the commas show that the information is extra.
What cannot be used with a preceding noun as an antecedent.
Whom is the object form and would leave the clause without a subject.
Where replaces a place preposition, and is a lawyer is not a place.

questions.explanation:
A clause about the same person as the main clause is the case where the comma matters most. Without it, the reader might think the two mentions referred to different people.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The car, ___ engine overheated, needed repairs.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a thing with a possessive.

options.feedback: Correct! The engine belongs to the car, and whose is the pronoun that expresses that link.
Which would refer to a thing, and the antecedent the car is a thing, but it cannot express the possessive relationship.
What cannot be preceded by a noun antecedent.
Who refers to people, and the antecedent is the car.

questions.explanation:
Whose applies to inanimate as well as animate antecedents. The car whose engine overheated shows ownership rather than identity.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The director, ___ can pay for the trip, refused to sign it.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a modal that does not change.

options.feedback: Correct! Modal verbs keep their form in any relative clause, defining or not.
Could would be the reported form, and this clause is not inside a reported statement.
A future form would change the meaning from present ability to a future possibility.
Must would express a deduction or an obligation, and the original is a plain claim about ability.

questions.explanation:
A modal is the same whatever the clause does. A non-defining clause with a modal keeps the modal exactly as it appears in the direct statement.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The witnesses, ___ the police, gave a detailed description.
questions.context: A non-defining clause in a sentence with a past perfect.

options.feedback: Correct! The formal object pronoun after a comma is the correct form for a non-defining object clause.
Which refers to things, and the antecedent is the witnesses.
Who cannot be an object, and the preposition the police needs a direct object.
That is excluded from non-defining clauses.

questions.explanation:
One of the clearest uses of whom is a non-defining clause ending in a preposition, because there is no other way to express the object formally.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: San Pedro Sula, ___ I was born, has grown very fast.
questions.context: A non-defining clause attached to a place name.

options.feedback: Correct! Where replaces in which and the clause then has its own subject I and verb was born.
Which would refer to a thing and cannot replace a place preposition with a full verb clause.
That cannot replace a preposition, and the clause has its own verb.
What cannot be used with a proper noun as an antecedent.

questions.explanation:
In a non-defining clause about a place, where is the natural choice because the clause has its own subject and verb. In which is the formal alternative.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: He missed the last bus, ___ meant he had to walk home.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a whole clause with a negative.

options.feedback: Correct! The non-defining which refers to the whole clause and the comma marks the consequence as extra.
It has no antecedent, because the preceding words are a clause rather than a noun.
That would restrict the bus and is not available in a non-defining clause.
This cannot introduce a relative clause at all.

questions.explanation:
A whole-clause which is a standard way of adding a comment. The comma is essential, because without it the reader would expect a noun to follow.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The university, ___ students live on campus, has a new library.
questions.context: A non-defining clause with a possessive pronoun about a university.

options.feedback: Correct! Whose links the university to its students, and it works with organisations.
Which could refer to the university, but it cannot connect the university to its students in a possessive way.
Who refers to people, and the antecedent is the university.
What cannot be used after a noun antecedent.

questions.explanation:
Whose is not limited to people. Institutions, objects and places all take whose when the relationship is one of belonging or ownership.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: "She lives in France, ___ speaks four languages," he said. He said that she lived in France, ___ spoke four languages.
questions.context: A non-defining clause reported in the past.

options.feedback: Correct! Both present simple verbs backshift to the past simple, and the non-defining clause keeps its pronoun.
Keeping the present would require a present reporting verb, and he said is in the past.
A past perfect would backshift twice, and present simple only takes one step back.
The first clause is not shifted at all, which leaves the two clauses in inconsistent tenses.

questions.explanation:
Backshift applies inside a non-defining clause exactly as it does in the main one. Each verb moves one step back independently of the other.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: The report, ___ three committees reviewed, will be published next week.
questions.context: A non-defining clause about a thing with a verb of its own.

options.feedback: Correct! Which is the subject of the clause, which has its own passive verb and agent.
That is not used in a non-defining clause and would wrongly restrict the report.
Whom is the object form, and three committees is the subject of the clause here.
Whose expresses possession, and the relationship here is that of agent to action.

questions.explanation:
A non-defining clause can hold a complete passive structure of its own, with its own subject, verb and by phrase.
---
questions.subject: ingles

questions.statement: My aunt, ___ is a doctor, ___ teaches at the local clinic, is coming to visit.
questions.context: Two non-defining clauses attached to the same noun.

options.feedback: Correct! Each non-defining clause repeats the full pronoun, and each is separated by its own comma.
That cannot introduce a non-defining clause, and the mixed usage would break the parallel structure.
Which cannot refer to the person who is the antecedent of the first clause.
Joining the clauses with and would produce a different structure, and the two commas would no longer mark separate clauses.

questions.explanation: Each non-defining clause is independent and repeats its own pronoun. The commas around them tell the reader where one extra piece of information ends and the next begins.
questions.subject: ingles
